results.message: How did someone join your community? What was baptism actually like?

voice_event.speaker: pahc
voice_event.text:
Before anything else came the teaching. We taught the Two Ways: a way of life and a way of death, and there is a great difference between the two ways. The Way of Life began with love of God and neighbor, and with this: do not do to another what you would not want done to you. It named what that meant plainly - not to murder, commit adultery, steal, or bear false witness; not to turn away from someone in want, but to share what you had rather than call anything only your own. The Way of Death was laid out by contrast, a list of what the Way of Life rejects.

Once that teaching had been given, the person preparing would be baptized. In running water if it could be found, but standing water if not, and if neither was available, water poured three times over the head, into the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Before the water, both the one baptizing and the one being baptized fasted - the one being baptized for one or two days beforehand, and any others who were able joined them. Only after the water could a person come to the table.

We should say plainly: this is the path one of our own communities' manuals lays out. We do not know how far this exact practice reached beyond that community. And there is something else we need to tell you honestly. One among us, Hermas, reports being taught that God granted one further chance for repentance after baptism, for those who had fallen into serious sin - offered then, before that door closed for good. So the water was not spoken of as though it made a person incapable of falling afterward. It marked entry. What came after it was a life still being formed.

sources.original_wording: There are two ways, one of life and one of death; but a great difference between the two ways. The way of life, then, is this: First, thou shalt love God who made thee; second, thy neighbour as thyself; and all things whatsoever thou wouldst should not occur to thee, thou also to another do not do.
sources.spoken_rendering: There are two ways: one of life and one of death, and there is a great difference between the two ways. The way of life is this. First, you shall love God, who made you; second, your neighbor as yourself. And whatever you would not want to happen to you, do not do to another.

sources.label: A freedman in Rome named Hermas reports receiving a series of visions, delivered through an elderly woman who is later revealed to be the Church herself, teaching that God has granted one further chance for repentance after baptism, before that door closes.

sources.author: Hermas (Rome; names himself as narrator and recipient of the visions in his own text)
sources.work: The Shepherd of Hermas; composite, multi-stage composition roughly 90-150 CE (Brox, Leutzsch, Osiek) - no single date can be assigned to the whole work; the traditional mid-2nd-century date rests partly on the Muratorian Fragment's 'brother of Pius' claim, itself undercut if Sundberg/Hahneman's 4th-century-Eastern dating of the Fragment is right
sources.locus: Vision 2.4.1 (the old woman who is the Church); Vision 2.4.3 (Clement and Grapte); Vision 3 (the woman growing younger)

figures_used.bridge_line: A freedman in Rome who wrote down his own visions - about failure, doubt, and whether mercy is used up.

dates.display: the Shepherd was composed c. 90-150, possibly in stages
dates.note: these bound the WORK, not the man - his own dates are not attested
